name: com.eancheck/barcode-tools
title: EAN Check barcode and shipping tools
description: GS1 barcodes, check digits, freight class, CBM, Julian dates and shelf life, worked out from input.

tools.name: calculate_check_digits
tools.description: Add the GS1 check digit to GTIN numbers that are missing it (7, 11, 12 or 13 digits become GTIN-8, UPC-A, EAN-13 or GTIN-14). One number per line or comma separated.

codes.description: Numbers without their check digit, one per line

tools.name: validate_gtins
tools.description: Check complete GTIN, EAN, UPC and ITF-14 numbers: says for each one whether the check digit is right and which GTIN length it is.

codes.description: Complete numbers, one per line or comma separated

tools.name: identify_code
tools.description: Find out what kind of code a string is: GTIN, ISBN, ISSN, SSCC, GLN, GS1-128 data, GS1 Digital Link, VIN, IMEI, ASIN, Amazon LPN or FNSKU, with its check digit status.

code.description: The code exactly as printed or scanned

tools.name: check_amazon_code
tools.description: Read the code from an Amazon sticker: tells an LPN (License Plate Number) from an FNSKU, ASIN, FBA box label, Amazon Logistics tracking number or UPC/EAN, and explains each part. It cannot look up which product a code belongs to.

code.description: The code as printed on the sticker, e.g. LPN RR AB1234567

tools.name: convert_upc_e
tools.description: Convert a UPC-E (6, 7 or 8 digits) to the full 12-digit UPC-A, or a UPC-A to UPC-E when one of the four GS1 zero-suppression rules fits. Checks the check digit.

code.description: A UPC-E or a UPC-A, digits only

tools.name: freight_class
tools.description: Work out the density (pounds per cubic foot) and the freight class of a US LTL shipment on the NMFC density scale with 13 steps, in force since 2025-07-19. Each line is one piece size: length x width x height x weight of one piece, and optionally x number of pieces. Up to 20 lines. A malformed line or unit gets an error, not a class.

lines.description: One line per piece size, as LxWxHxWEIGHT or LxWxHxWEIGHTxPIECES (4 or 5 values), for example 48x40x48x500 or 24x18x12x30x3. The separator inside a line is x, X, × or *. Separate lines with a new line, a semicolon, or a comma followed by the next line (48x40x48x500, 24x18x12x30x3). A decimal comma inside a value is read as a decimal point (47,5 is 47.5). At most 20 lines: put pieces of the same size on one line with a piece count.

size_unit.description: Unit of the sizes: in or cm (also inch, inches, centimeter(s), centimetre(s); any case). Default in.

weight_unit.description: Unit of the weights: lb or kg (also lbs, pound(s), kgs, kilogram(s); any case). Default lb.

tools.name: cbm_calculator
tools.description: Work out the volume of a shipment in cubic metres (CBM) and cubic feet, how much of a 20 ft, 40 ft, 40 ft high cube and 45 ft high cube dry container it fills, how many pieces of one size go into each container by size, and, when weights are given, the chargeable weight for air freight (divisor 6000), courier (5000) and sea freight LCL (1 m3 = 1000 kg). Each line is one piece size: length x width x height, optionally x quantity, optionally x weight of one piece. Up to 20 lines. A malformed line, unit or divisor gets an error, not a volume.

lines.description: One line per piece size, as LxWxH, LxWxHxQUANTITY or LxWxHxQUANTITYxWEIGHT (3 to 5 values), for example 60x40x50x10x12 for ten cartons of 60 by 40 by 50 at 12 each. The separator inside a line is x, X, × or *. Separate lines with a new line or a semicolon (a comma followed by a space and the next line works too). A comma between digits inside a value is a decimal comma (47,5 is 47.5), with two exceptions that get an error, not a volume: a comma followed by exactly three digits (1,250 could be 1250 or 1.25: send one of them without the comma), and a comma that could also be a line break. Write decimals with a point to be safe. WEIGHT is the weight of one piece. At most 20 lines: put pieces of the same size on one line with a quantity.

size_unit.description: Unit of the sizes: mm, cm, m, in or ft (also the full names; any case). Default cm.

weight_unit.description: Unit of the weights: kg or lb (also kgs, kilogram(s), lbs, pound(s); any case). Default kg.

divisor.description: Optional. The carrier's own volumetric divisor in cubic centimetres per kilogram, for example 4000. Adds one more chargeable weight to the answer. From 100 to 100000.

may_turn.description: Optional. true when a piece may be laid on its side for the count by size. Default false: the third value of each line stays the height, as for a loaded pallet or a this-side-up carton.

tools.name: julian_date
tools.description: Convert a day-number date code (a "Julian date" on packaging: DDD, YDDD, YYDDD, CYYDDD or YYYYDDD) or an astronomical Julian Date (JD, MJD) to a calendar date, or a calendar date to every code form. Give `code` or `date`, not both. Dates from 1583-01-01 to 9999-12-31. A code that is not a date gets an error and a hint, not a guess. An answer for a code with a year in it says how old the date is, counted from `today`; for a three-digit code, the day this year once it has come.

code.description: One code as printed: 3 digits (day of year, as on egg cartons), 4 (last digit of year + day), 5 (two-digit year + day), 6 (JD Edwards CYYDDD) or 7 (four-digit year + day). A separator between year and day is allowed (25-319, 2025-319, 2025.319). Letters around one group of digits are left out ("LOT 25319 B2" reads 25319); two groups of digits ("042 155") are refused as two codes. For an astronomy number send the decimals (2460994.5) or put JD or MJD in front (MJD 61360). One code per call.

date.description: A Gregorian calendar date as YYYY-MM-DD, from 1583-01-01 to 9999-12-31, to get its day number and codes.

today.description: Optional, YYYY-MM-DD, from 1583-01-01 to 9999-12-31 (default: today in UTC). The date a one-digit or two-digit year is read against, and the date the age of the result is counted from. A two-digit year is read as a year from today minus 89 years to today plus 10, moved to stay inside 1583 to 9999; a one-digit year as the latest year ending in that digit, not after this year. Set it to the date the item was handled when the code is old.

tools.name: shelf_life_calculator
tools.description: Work out an expiry date, a production date or a shelf life from the other two, and how much of the shelf life is left on a check date. Send two of `production`, `shelf_life` and `expiry`, or only `expiry` for the days left. Months and years are calendar months: a day that does not exist in the new month becomes its last day (31 January + 1 month = 28 February), and the answer says so. Dates are read as packs print them, GS1 dates included. An expiry given as month and year is the last day of the month, a production date given as month and year the first day (a GS1 date with day 00 stays the last day, as GS1 defines it). Optional `minimum` checks a minimum life left, as a share (2/3, 70%) or a time (105 days). Dates from 1900 to 2199. The tool does not know how long a product keeps.

production.description: The production date: 2026-03-15, 15 Mar 2026, 15.03.2026, 03/15/2026 (see `date_order`) or a GS1 date such as (11)260315. Month and year only (MFG 03/2026) means the first day of the month; a GS1 date with day 00 stays the last day, as GS1 defines it.

shelf_life.description: The shelf life with a unit: 540 days, 12 weeks, 18 months, 2 years, or 2 years 6 months. Whole numbers only; 1,000 and 1 000 are read as one thousand.

expiry.description: The expiry or best-before date as printed: 2027-09-15, EXP 11/2027 (month and year mean the last day of the month), BBE 30.11.2027, or a GS1 date such as (17)271100 (day 00 means the last day of the month). Sent alone, it gives the days left.

find.description: Optional: what to work out. Default: the one of the three that is not sent. Do not send the value of the field being found.

check_date.description: Optional, the date to count the days left from, as YYYY-MM-DD (default: today in UTC), such as the day the goods arrive.

minimum.description: Optional minimum life left: a share (2/3, 1/2, 70%) or a time (105 days, 3 months).

date_type.description: Optional GS1 AI for the printed forms: 17 expiry or use-by (default), 15 best before, 16 sell by.

includes_production_day.description: Optional, default false. True when the shelf life counts the production day as day 1, so the expiry is one day earlier.

date_order.description: Optional, how to read a date with slashes such as 05/06/2026: dmy (5 June, default) or mdy (May 6). Dates with dots are always day first. Send YYYY-MM-DD to avoid the question.

tools.name: convert_isbn
tools.description: Convert an ISBN-10 to ISBN-13 or back, with the check digit recalculated and the hyphenated form. ISBN-13 starting with 979 has no ISBN-10.

isbn.description: An ISBN-10 or ISBN-13, with or without hyphens

tools.name: repair_gtin
tools.description: Recover a GTIN with unreadable digits: mark each unknown digit with ? or * and get every number that passes the GS1 check digit.

code.description: The GTIN with ? or * for each unknown digit, e.g. 59012341?3457

tools.name: parse_gs1
tools.description: Split GS1 data (GS1-128, GS1 DataMatrix, Digital Link) into its Application Identifiers, with the name of each AI and any format error.

data.description: GS1 data such as (01)09506000134352(17)271231(10)ABC123, FNC1 form or a Digital Link URL

tools.name: make_barcode
tools.description: Draw a print-ready barcode and return it as SVG (or EPS) in millimetres, plus a link that opens it in the generator. Types: upc-a, ean-13, ean-8, itf-14, code-128, code-39, code-93, interleaved-2-of-5, codabar, msi, pharmacode, data-matrix, pdf417, aztec. GS1 retail types use magnification 80 to 200 (percent).

value.description: The data. GTIN types accept the number without its check digit.

magnification.description: GS1 types only: size in percent, 100 is the standard size

x_mm.description: Other types: narrowest bar or module width in mm

gs1.description: Data Matrix only: treat the value as GS1 data like (01)09506000134352(17)271231

tools.name: barcode_size
tools.description: Give the printed size of a barcode type at a GS1 magnification (retail and carton types) or an X-dimension, with the GS1 allowed range.

x_mm.description: Other types: narrowest bar width in mm
